cost.description:
Direct costs are 15,68€/hour (more information on fees is available in 'BIGAN>Services>Fees' https://bigan.iacs.es/en/services/fees) and include data request processing, a) data mining, ETL processing, and c) security and quality assurance.
The service includes defining queries and extracting information on available information sources, extracting the requested data, and completing the ETL processes to comply with the requested common data model specification.

The global cost of a typical data request for a population-level research question is usually under 2000 euros, and the data is usually served in approximately three weeks.

Indirect costs are associated with the data management and data analysis to respond to the research question after the data request is served and consider only the person/time of the data manager and data scientists assigned to the task.

data_quality_assurance: Set up of scientific and technical committee
Use of tools for automatic checks
Consistency verified with data models and standards

BIGAN has a data quality assurance system for data processing to enable the secondary use of health data in Aragon (Spain).  In addition, we implement our own data quality assessment and assurance procedures within the BY-COVID baseline use case, aiming to provide insight into the impact of data quality in interpreting the research outcomes and producing high-quality research. Those procedures include the assessment of the information requirements and the data model specification by a scientific and technical committee, the implementation of an automatic data quality check (i.e. exploratory data analysis - EDA) on the original dataset of each participant on-site, the implementation of data conformance and consistency checking following the common data model specification, and a final missing values assessment on core variables to inform decisions on imputation requirements.
dataset.description:
The CONCEPT-STROKE public health cohort in Aragon links selected variables from primary care or hospital admissions for Acute Ischemic Stroke (AIS), covering a global population for the region of approximately 1.3 million lives.

This cohort includes all patients admitted to hospital due to Acute Ischemic Stroke (AIS) in a public hospital in Aragon (Spain) and complementary information on patient attributes (e.g., comorbidities, prescribed stroke drug) and patient dependency measurements (e.g., Modified Rankin Scale (mRS), and Barthel index).

Original data is maintained and updated daily by BIGAN (Health Data Space in Aragon). 

A common data model specification with the required information to achieve the expected results of the research question is provided as supporting documentation at  https://zenodo.org/record/8012966 - Common Data Model Specification.
BIGAN provides pseudonymised data in compliance with the baseline use case data model specification after the data request is processed and granted by the Aragon Ethical Research Committee.

host.description:
BIGAN is a technological platform that integrates all data from the health system for healthcare managers, educators, and researchers.

BIGAN is the Department of Health of the Government of Aragon's Big Data project. It was created to improve healthcare using data routinely collected within Aragon's public health system. The project's development has been entrusted to the Aragon Institute of Health Sciences (IACS).
The project aims to integrate all data collected within the health system on a technological platform, where it can be analysed by healthcare professionals, managers, educators, and researchers. The ultimate goal is to improve the healthcare system and the health of residents in Aragon through data observation. Collecting, analysing, and sharing information between all stakeholders is vital to achieve this.
BIGAN is a technological infrastructure owned by the Government of Aragon, managed by the Aragon Institute of Health Sciences, and financed by the Department of Health and the Aragon Health Service, in which information from health information systems and other useful sources is captured, anonymized, safeguarded, and analysed, to fulfil BIGAN’s objectives.
BIGAN guarantees the protection and anonymization of data at all times. Researchers who use the data will never have access to any personal information that would enable identification of either the patient or their environment.
BIGAN and the project's development is regulated by ORDER SAN/1355/2018, of August 1, published in the Official Gazette of Aragon on August 22 and in which the terms of its creation are established.

dataset.preservation_statement: BIGAN has a regional mandate from the government of Aragon to curate and maintain original data requests (and related ETL queries) in the long term and report on the re-use of health data for research purposes.

security_and_privacy.description:
Original data is de-identified and pseudonymised using a Hash function before being extracted from BIGAN (Data holder and secure processing environment) and then served for research purposes encrypted and compressed, requiring a secure password to decompress the files.
The data request process includes a feasibility and security assessment of the information requirements specified in the data model, which considers data minimization to achieve the research objectives.

dmp.description:
This publication corresponds to the Data Management Plan (DMP) for the "CONCEPT-STROKE: Effectiveness and efficiency of acute ischemic stroke care pathways in five Spanish regions" project.

CONCEPT-STROKE aims to estimate the effectiveness and efficiency of the care pathway followed by acute ischaemic stroke patients using real-world data routinely collected by five healthcare systems in Spain. This project builds on a two-stage design: a cross-sectional data mining design followed by a quasi-experimental design comparing interventions on acute ischaemic stroke. 
  • Stage I: the pathway of care as such, as it happens in real life and the propensity for a patient to follow a specific path.
  • Stage II: patients’ survival at 30 days and 6 months after admission to an emergency room. 
Below is a brief structured description of the research question, the proposed study design, and the cohort definition. 
Research Question: “What is the effectiveness and efficiency of the care pathway followed by patients with acute ischemic stroke?”
Income: patients who have suffered an acute ischemic stroke  
Outcome: the care pathway followed by acute ischaemic stroke patients and patients’ survival at 1 year after admission to an emergency room. 
Study Design: An observational retrospective longitudinal study to discover and compare actual care paths with the theoretical pathway and with those present in the five regions and a survival analysis to predict health outcomes within each path.
Cohort definition: all patients 18 years or older admitted to hospital due to acute ischemic stroke.
  • Inclusion criteria: Patients 18 years or older admitted to emergency care services (or with an unplanned admission to hospital) with a principal diagnosis of Acute Ischemic Stroke (AIS) during the study period.
  • Exlusión criteria: Patients 17 years or younger or patients with a diagnosis of acute hemorrhagic stroke or with other non-specific stroke diagnoses (i.e. transient ischemic attack - TIA)
  • Study period: From 01-01-2010 until 31-12-2022

project.description:
CONCEPT-STROKE is part of CONCEPT, a coordinated research initiative including five projects
under the umbrella of REDISSEC, the Spanish Research Network on Health Services Research
and Chronic Conditions (www.redissec.com). CONCEPT projects seek to analyse the
effectiveness and efficiency of the care provided to patients with diabetes, atrial fibrillation,
breast cancer and ischaemic stroke in eight Spanish healthcare systems. Aims: In Stroke care,
we aim to show the relevance of care pathways on the health outcomes and efficiency of
Stroke care.
